policies.label: Visa required; stay unconfirmed
policies.n: Ordinary Czech Republic passport: a visa is required for a short tourist visit. This establishes visa duty, not routine issuance or admission. The permitted stay and electronic or exceptional arrival eligibility are not established by this nationality-specific evidence.

policies.label: Visa required; stay unconfirmed
policies.n: Irish citizens require a visa. Use an Irish passport, not a passport card; DFA specifies six months validity beyond intended departure. The permitted stay and electronic or exceptional arrival eligibility are unconfirmed. Visa duty does not guarantee issuance or admission.

policies.label: eVisa; Phu Quoc exception
policies.n: For ordinary tourism beyond the separate Phu Quoc island-only exemption, obtain a visa; the government makes eVisas available to citizens of all countries and territories. Use approved eVisa border gates and comply with the period actually granted; the source’s up-to-90-day visa validity is not a guaranteed stay. The June 2026 bilateral ordinary-passport waiver is not operative by 9 October 2026: it was submitted for parliamentary approval on 24 September, entered the parliamentary initial stage on 5 October, and Article 10 requires 30 days after the last notification of completed domestic procedures. The existing diplomatic/official exemption does not cover ordinary tourism. The separately documented Phu Quoc island-only concession is up to 30 days; it does not permit mainland tourism, and the qualifying island itinerary must be satisfied.
